<RuleLanguageLinks current="javascript" languages={[{"id":"javascript","label":"JavaScript (and super languages)","href":"/linter/rules/no-immediate-mutation/javascript/"}]} />

:::caution
This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.9`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/noImmediateMutation`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- Sources: 
  - Inspired from [`unicorn/no-immediate-mutation`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn/blob/main/docs/rules/no-immediate-mutation.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"noImmediateMutation": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Disallow changing a value right after it is created.

Adding to an array, object, `Set`, or `Map` in the statement after it is created splits its
initial contents in two. The same goes for declaring a variable and assigning it in the next
statement. Put the contents in the initial value instead.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
const array = [1, 2];
array.push(3, 4);
```

### Valid

```js
const array = [1, 2, 3, 4];

const object = { foo: 1, bar: 2, ...other };

const set = new Set([1, 2, 3]);

const map = new Map([
    ["foo", 1],
    ["bar", 2],
]);

const items = [];
items.push(items.length);

let foo = 1;
```
